excerpt: Marker Learning offered remote learning and attention disability evaluations and now develops Marker Method, an adaptive clinical assessment battery for school psychologists. Funding and alternatives.
content:
Marker Learning is a New York company that set out to make learning disability evaluations, such as testing for dyslexia, faster and cheaper. AlleyWatch described it in 2021 as a telepsychology platform where psychologists and learning disability specialists give evaluations remotely through the company's own technology, designed with Johns Hopkins psychologists. Pulse 2.0 reported in 2023 that it served people aged 6 to 50, delivered a diagnostic report within a month that could support accommodations at school, at work or for standardised tests, and partnered with school districts to support special-education caseloads. Its founders said private evaluations elsewhere can cost up to $14,000 with waitlists of more than two years.

The company was co-founded by Stefan Bauer, the CEO, and Emily Yudofsky. Bauer told AlleyWatch that he was close to failing at school until a learning disability evaluation diagnosed his dyslexia, after which he went on to Yale and McKinsey. Marker raised a seed round of about $4 million in 2021 led by Primary, with Divergent Investments, Night Ventures and Operator Partners. In February 2023 it raised a $15 million Series A led by Andreessen Horowitz, with the venture arm of Richard Branson's Virgin Group, existing investors and athletes including NBA champion Danny Green and WNBA champion Jewell Loyd, Pulse 2.0 reported. It said at the time that its school partnerships reached 1 million students and that it was adding tutoring and coaching.

Marker's website now focuses on Marker Method, a clinical assessment battery for clinicians such as school psychologists. It covers academic, cognitive, psychomotor and language domains, chooses from 37 tests based on the referral and the student's answers, scores in real time, and adjusts norms for students' exposure to English. The site says a norming study is under way and it is recruiting partner developers before launch.

No price is published for Marker Method. Earlier coverage described Marker's evaluations as a fraction of the cost of traditional ones without giving a figure we could confirm.

This page is research, not medical or educational advice. Facts come from the pages listed under Sources.
